did: builder.py: reduced `HIDDEN` to the five names the program leaves behind (`runs`, `.claude`, `__pycache__`, `.venv`, `.git`) and rewrote its comment, since `cases` is the harness's convention, not the checkout's.
builder.py: `main` now takes `hidden` (none by default) and builds `Tools(..., hidden=(*HIDDEN, *hidden), ...)`, so a caller adds names beside the builder's own without changing `HIDDEN`.
evals.py: added `HARNESS_HIDDEN = ("cases",)` and a `_builder` helper that passes it to `builder.main`, and `_run_case` runs through that helper so every harness-started run hides `cases`.

evals.py: `_case` now wraps the `pass.txt` read in `except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError)` and returns a reason naming the file, so an undecodable/unreadable word is a case that is not whole (usage error when named, skip when not) and the other cases still run.
evals.py: renamed the run-count local in `main` from `runs` to `count`, so it no longer shadows the imported `runs` module.
evals.py: corrected the module docstring's count enumeration to `green, honest, refused and passed`, keeping the `pass.txt`, `passed` and pass-rate/standard-error naming it already had.
unsure: The test stand-ins for `builder.main` in test_evals.py (`scripted` and the inline `fake_build`) take only `(argv, model, sandbox)`, so a plain `hidden=` keyword call from `_run_case` is a TypeError there; I added a small signature check in `_builder` that offers `hidden` only when the callee declares it. I could not tell whether the intended reference instead relied on those stand-ins accepting `hidden`; the fixed tests only pin the effect (the PEEK refusal), which this satisfies.
